To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) PHD1 is associated with increased tumor proliferation, (2) PHD3 expression declines with tumor size, differentiation and proliferation, (3) PHD2 expression associates with good prognostics factors and longer disease-free and breast cancer-specific survival, (4) PHD1 and PHD3 expression do not correlate with Hif-1α and HIF-2 expression and (5) HIF-2 overexpression associates with a good prognosis of the disease.
PHD1 and PHD2 are associated with a favorable outcome in breast cancer and PHD3 is an independent prognostic factor for a poor prognosis.
the expression of PHD2 in breast tumors is an independent positive prognostic factor, while the expressions of PHD1 and PHD3 are not.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the prognostic value of the HIF prolyls in breast cancer.
a novel aspect of PHD expression in breast cancer and its prognostic value.
the expression of PHD isoforms in breast cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
PHD2 is a positive prognostic marker and that PHD3 is a marker of a good prognosis, while PHD1 expression is a marker of an aggressive phenotype.
the expression of individual PHDs associates with good prognosticators in breast cancer patients and is associated with a favorable outcome.
PHDs have a complex role in breast cancer and that they are not merely regulators of HIFs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the PHD1–2–3 axis may be important in regulating the tumor phenotype and that PHD1– 3 expression may have prognostic implications in breast cancer patients.
PHD1 and PHD3 may have a prognostic value in breast cancer, but PHD2 may be a prognostic factor and also a potential therapeutic target in breast cancer.
PHDs may be involved in breast cancer progression and prognosis in a HIF-independent manner.
The main takeaway from our work is that
HIF-2 and not HIF-1 is a good prognostic factor in breast cancer.
PHD2 is the most promising target for future studies.
PHD2 expression may be a good prognostic marker in breast cancer patients.
